questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: If your car's rear end starts skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front of your car in line with the rear and straightens your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. It is unsafe and illegal to turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:

options.text: Stay aware of what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay aware of what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle. Look to the front, sides, and rear to spot problems early. This lets you change speed or position before danger occurs.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Begin to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Sound a sharp horn blast when a child or pedestrian is about to enter the street in front of your vehicle. This alerts them to the danger.

questions.question: Which describes a defensive driver's thinking?

options.text: Other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect no courtesy and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you predict what other drivers might do wrong and prepare to handle their mistakes.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the traffic speed, signal, and:

options.text: Expect traffic to make room for you since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, signal, then merge into the gap when safe. Watch other traffic and do not expect drivers to clear the lane for you.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Avoid the brakes and let the car slow down naturally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly on snow or ice. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many cars are passing you on the right. If a driver behind you wants to go faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so you don't slow down traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let cars pass.
Move into the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to drive fast, pass, or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than other traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: You should always travel at:

options.text: The speed of cars around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a leading cause of crashes. It does not save time and often causes drivers to make risky choices.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol for drivers under 21. Any trace of alcohol in your system results in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: On a highway with a dashed white line between lanes:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. They alert drivers to watch for bicycles, animals, and pedestrians that may cross the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Get ready. Traffic will merge into your lane.
Always stop.
A divided highway is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready. Traffic will merge into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right into your lane. Be prepared to let them in safely.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels facing straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. If your brakes fail, the car will roll off the road instead of into traffic.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines are used on streets and highways to:

options.text: Mark no passing zones.
Separate lanes moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when standing water is on the road. At 35 mph and below, tires can push water away. Above 35 mph, tires lose grip and slide on the water like skis.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit for the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic that is already on the freeway.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Use only your rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Use only your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Check multiple times and keep watching both ahead and beside you.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, drivers should:

options.text: Let entering traffic go first.
Let traffic already in the roundabout go first.
Drive clockwise around the circle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic already in the roundabout go first.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic light. Traffic moves counterclockwise around a center island. Enter from the right and yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A divided highway is ending.
A divided highway is beginning.
The road will be slippery ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is beginning.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway begins ahead. Stay to the right of the median divider.

questions.question: Highway pavement is most slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for several hours.
When rain just starts.
When it has been raining for 1 to 2 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with the rain and create a slick coating.

questions.question: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep your eyes on the center line of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Don't look at bright headlights. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road. Then continue looking ahead to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: If dust or smoke makes it hard to see other vehicles, drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights when conditions block your view. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: To turn quickly, place your hands:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Put both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: Which statement is true about roadwork zones?

options.text: Traffic fines in work zones are the same as normal fines.
You must slow down for work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down in all work zones. Watch for equipment and be ready to stop. Safe driving in work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, and workers.

questions.question: Give right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians crossing in any marked or unmarked crosswalk. For safety, give pedestrians the right-of-way whenever they cross any street.

questions.question: In rainy weather, be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has rained all day.
A half hour after rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with rain to create a slippery surface.
